facts: The revolt of 1857 is called India's First War of Independence.
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
Gandhi led the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), the Salt March to Dandi (1930) and Quit India (1942).
India became independent on 15 August 1947, with partition into India and Pakistan.
Methods included non-violence (ahimsa), boycotts and swadeshi.

narration.text: India's struggle for freedom from British rule lasted about ninety years.

events.text: A great revolt against British rule

narration.text: In eighteen fifty-seven, a large revolt against British rule began.
In eighteen eighty-five, the Indian National Congress was formed.
In nineteen thirty, Gandhi led the Salt March to Dandi.
On fifteenth August nineteen forty-seven, India became independent.
Gandhi led the struggle through non-violence.
People boycotted British goods and wore Indian khadi cloth.
Huge peaceful marches united millions of Indians.
In nineteen seventeen, Gandhi supported indigo farmers in Champaran.
In nineteen twenty, Indians boycotted British schools, courts and goods.
In nineteen thirty, he walked to Dandi to make salt, breaking the salt law.
In nineteen forty-two, the Quit India Movement demanded that the British leave.

scenes.heading: Step 4: Why freedom came in 1947
items: Britain weakened by World War II

narration.text: Decades of mass movements made British rule very hard to continue.
The Second World War left Britain weak and in debt.
In nineteen forty-six, Indian sailors of the Royal Navy rebelled.
Independence came with partition into India and Pakistan.
Leaders chose peaceful methods that ordinary people could join.
Boycotting British cloth hurt British trade and promoted Indian goods.
In the Salt March, Gandhi walked to Dandi to break the salt law peacefully.
In 1942 the Quit India movement demanded that the British leave.
